learningObjectives: Integrate a new feature of the system under test into an existing TestSheet.
Determine when a new Attribute only needs a value added to existing combinations, versus when it needs entirely new combinations.
Inspect affected lower and upper combinations after a data-model change and use the selected coverage method consistently.
Inspect Requirement links, add missing links and recalculate coverage after extending the design.

elements.description: Applications evolve — new features get added to the system under test after a TestSheet already exists. When a new feature affects existing test data, the TestSheet needs a new Attribute (and its Instances) integrated into the structure that's already in place, without starting over.

Create the new Attribute wherever it logically fits in the existing structure — it can be added right alongside Attributes that already have combinations, even if that means the existing combination set now needs to account for it.

Inspect combinations at every affected level. Fill missing baseline values where appropriate, then complete or propagate uncovered variations according to the chosen method and constraints. The documented Complete Instances command adds uncombined combinations without duplicating existing ones; Propagate Instance(s) adds chosen combinations without applying a combinatorial method.

elements.title: Two possible updates
items: Fill the new baseline value in an existing baseline row when it represents the same scenario. This alone does not cover the new alternatives.

Reassess coverage using All Combinations, Orthogonal, Pairwise or Linear Expansion as appropriate. Additional rows depend on the method, existing coverage and Relations; there is no universal one-row-per-new-value rule.

elements.text: Inspect missing values and Instance Usage at the affected levels. For explicit propagation, select the source Instance(s), Ctrl-select the higher-level Instances object, and use Propagate Instance(s). Inspect the result; propagation is not a claim that all coverage requirements are satisfied.

bulletPoints: Adding a new option to an Attribute doesn't automatically mean a new TestCase — it depends on whether the combinatorial method requires one.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Independent worked example: extending shipping choices

elements.description: Independent Quilyn example, not a verified Academy exercise: assume an unconstrained Linear Expansion design with Ground as the shipping baseline and two previously uncovered alternatives, Next Day Air and Second Day Air. Pickup has N/A shipping. Real business constraints must be modeled rather than inferred from these labels.

Fill Ground in the existing checkout baseline and N/A where shipping does not apply. In this example, neither air-shipping alternative is represented yet. Add two checkout scenarios, each varying only the shipping choice while keeping the other fields at their valid StraightThrough baselines.

At the TestSheet level, inspect existing rows and select appropriate checkout data. Assume the two new checkout alternatives are not represented there either: this simple Linear Expansion example adds two upper-level baseline variations, one for each checkout alternative. Other methods or Relations can require different combinations; there is no fixed original count of nine rows.

bulletPoints: Check affected lower-level combinations before upper-level coverage; retain existing valid scenarios and add only the combinations required by the selected method.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Inspect Requirement coverage and refresh calculations

elements.text: Inspect the links for new Instances rather than assuming coverage from a previously linked TestSheet. Drag any missing design Instances to their relevant Requirements to create substitutes. After adding executable tests and execution links, replace substitutes as appropriate and use Update Outdated Values when automatic calculation is disabled.

The Academy video and exercise files require access and have not been verified. Practice this documented workflow in your own workspace; independently inspect the resulting combinations, links and calculations.

examPitfalls.title: Updating only the TestSheet level
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Adding new Instances at the TestSheet level but forgetting the lower Attribute level (or vice versa) still has missing values for the new Attribute.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check missing values and usage at every affected level. Complete or propagate combinations and inspect resulting coverage; do not assume only the top-level design needs attention.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming every new option automatically needs a new TestCase
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Creating a brand-new Instance combination for every new option, even when it just fits into an existing row.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Filling the existing baseline can preserve that scenario. Reassess alternative coverage separately; the method and constraints determine whether additional combinations are necessary.

examPitfalls.title: Forgetting to re-link new Instances to Requirements
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming new Instances automatically inherit the Requirement links their TestSheet already had.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Inspect actual links and add missing Instance-to-Requirement links. Refresh outdated calculations; a prior TestSheet link alone is not evidence that the new scope is currently reflected.

practiceQuiz.scenario: For the existing StraightThrough scenario only, a new Attribute needs its default value filled in. Must this baseline scenario be duplicated solely because the Attribute was added?

options.text: Yes, always — any new Attribute automatically requires a new TestCase.
No — the value can be filled directly into the existing combination if it maps onto a row that already exists.
Only if the Attribute is set to BusinessRelevant = No.
Only if the new Attribute has no Instances.

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate maintaining the existing baseline from covering the new alternatives.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The existing baseline row can be completed with its new default. This does not establish coverage of other values; those must be assessed using the chosen method and constraints.

optionExplanations.A: A new column does not by itself require duplicating a valid baseline row.
optionExplanations.B: The existing baseline can be completed; alternative coverage remains a separate task.
optionExplanations.C: Business relevance is not a rule requiring duplication of the baseline.
optionExplanations.D: An Attribute without values does not provide the specified default for this scenario.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the independent unconstrained Linear Expansion example, two new Checkout alternatives are not covered by any current TestSheet row. To extend upper-level coverage while keeping all other Attributes at baseline, what should you add?

options.text: Two matching new TestSheet-level Instances must be added, selecting the corresponding new Checkout Instance.
The TestSheet must be deleted and rebuilt from scratch.
The Checkout Attribute must be converted into a Class.

practiceQuiz.hint: There are two uncovered checkout alternatives and this example varies one choice at a time.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Under these stated assumptions, add one upper-level row per uncovered Checkout alternative, retaining the other baseline selections. This count is not a rule for every method or relation-constrained design.

optionExplanations.A: The question states that no current upper-level row covers these alternatives; inspect and extend that coverage.
optionExplanations.B: Two baseline variations cover the two missing Checkout choices under this simple Linear Expansion assumption.
optionExplanations.C: The existing valid design can be extended without deleting the TestSheet.
optionExplanations.D: Classes enable reuse; converting the Attribute does not establish the missing upper-level coverage.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A tester finishes adding a new Attribute and its Instances, and updates all combinations at every level. What step do they still need to complete before this new coverage shows up on the project dashboard?

options.text: Inspect Requirement links, add any missing Instance links, and refresh outdated coverage calculations.
Convert the new Attribute into a Class.

practiceQuiz.hint: Design data, Requirement links and current calculated values are separate parts of the dashboard.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Check the actual Requirement links and add missing ones. Recalculate outdated values with Update Outdated Values when automatic calculation is off. Adding data alone is not evidence of a current coverage dashboard.

optionExplanations.A: New design data alone does not demonstrate that links and calculated dashboard values are current.
optionExplanations.B: This checks traceability and updates stale calculations instead of assuming inherited coverage.
optionExplanations.C: Class conversion supports shared data structures, not Requirement linking or recalculation.
optionExplanations.D: Arrange Instances reorganizes design data; it does not establish Requirement links or refresh coverage.

quickRecap.key: Where to add a new Attribute
quickRecap.value: Wherever it fits logically — even alongside Attributes with existing combinations.
Complete the existing baseline, then reassess alternative coverage using the method, existing combinations and Relations.
Inspect all affected levels; Complete Instances or Propagate Instance(s) serve different purposes.
Inspect links, add missing Instance-to-Requirement links and update outdated calculated values.
